issues.failure_explanation: On I^j, phi(t)=jh+delta^mu+(h-delta^mu)P(...). If h=delta^mu, this is constant jh+h, so phi is not strictly increasing. The numerical tests explicitly choose h=delta^mu, so the constructed inner functions are flat on intervals and psi_q' vanishes there, contradicting the strict monotonicity and derivative-vanishing claims.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require h>delta^mu (e.g., choose mu so delta^mu<h) or state non-strict monotonicity and adjust derivative claims.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised strict monotonicity of inner functions and the derivative nonvanishing claim fail for the parameter choice used in examples; Theorem Inner-Lemma's statement is false at equality.
issues.title: Strict monotonicity fails when h=delta^mu
issues.why_classification: A local parameter condition h>delta^mu restores strict monotonicity; the main approximation rate and method survive, though examples must be adjusted.

issues.failure_explanation: The y-values involve delta^mu and phi((1-q)delta), which need not be rational. From the formula, for interior centers a_q^j = h lambda·j + C_q |lambda|_1. Equality between different q reduces to a linear equation with an irrational coefficient (unless delta^mu is rational). One can choose delta,mu so the required ratio lambda1/lambda2 is irrational, yielding rationally independent lambda with equal images. Thus the proposition's cross-level distinctness is false.

failure_location.quote: Then the images   $a_q^{\bs j}$ of the Kolmogorov maps of $ \bs c_q^{\bs j}$ in \eqref{aqJaj} are all distinct.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the statement to fixed q or add a genericity/no-equality condition on lambda.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed separation property that all a_q^j are distinct for any rationally independent lambda is not valid; only distinctness for fixed q is generally supported.
issues.title: Proposition Cor:Dist is false for general rationally independent lambda
issues.why_classification: The proposition is false as stated and its proof is invalid; however, the main approximation theorem only uses row-wise distinctness at fixed q, so a weakened version preserves the core result.

issues.failure_explanation: From the condition one can only deduce lambda_j/lambda_{j+1} < tilde h, not the stronger tilde h/(1+tilde h). For example, with tilde h=0.5, lambda1=0.1, lambda2=1, lambda3=2.3, the condition holds (0.1<0.5 and 1.1/2.3<0.5), but lambda2/lambda3≈0.435>0.333≈0.5/1.5.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the inequality by the correct consequence lambda_j/lambda_{j+1}<tilde h.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed quantitative relation between consecutive lambda's is incorrect; the asymptotic statement lambda_p=O(N^{p-d}) may still hold.
issues.title: Remark Cond-lambda gives an incorrect ratio bound
issues.why_classification: The false inequality is in a remark and is not used in the main proof; a one-line correction fixes it.

issues.failure_explanation: The algorithm chooses the adjacent center with minimum image distance, which under eqref{lambdaPQ} is the coordinate with the smallest lambda. But Psi_q(x) includes deviations in all coordinates; deviations in coordinates with larger lambda can exceed the spacing in the chosen coordinate. Then t=Psi_q(x) need not lie between a_q^i and the selected neighbor, so the row interpolation g_q^{i_l}(t) is evaluated outside its defining interval (or with the wrong interval). The MainResult proof's bound |b_q^j - g_q(Psi_q(x))| <= |s_{k+1}-s_k| requires such bracketing. Thus the algorithm does not define a global outer function g_q or guarantee the claimed evaluation.

failure_location.quote:
a_q^{(i_1,\ldots,i_{l-1},i_l+\sigma^*, i_{l+1},\ldots, i_d)}=\min_{1\le k\le d}\big\{
 \big|a_q^{\bs i}-a_q^{\bs i+ \bs e_k} \big|,\, \big|a_q^{\bs i}-a_q^{\bs i-\bs e_k} \big|\big\},

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, the algorithm must select an interpolation row/interval that actually contains Psi_q(x) (e.g., interpolate along the dominant coordinate and prove the other coordinates' deviations are smaller) and define a consistent global C^2 g_q.
issues.overall_effect: The construction of g_q is not well-defined for arbitrary x, and the proof of the main approximation theorem is invalid.
issues.title: Outer-function row selection does not guarantee bracketing of Psi_q(x)
issues.why_classification: The defect affects the core outer-function construction and the main convergence proof; a repair requires a new argument or modified interpolation scheme.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
a_q^{(i_1,\ldots,i_{l-1},i_l+\sigma^*, i_{l+1},\ldots, i_d)}=\min_{1\le k\le d}\big\{
 \big|a_q^{\bs i}-a_q^{\bs i+ \bs e_k} \big|,\, \big|a_q^{\bs i}-a_q^{\bs i-\bs e_k} \big|\big\},

issues.failure_explanation: For an interior index i, the distances to i+e_k and i-e_k in the same coordinate k are equal (both are lambda_k h for interior rows). If this coordinate realizes the minimum, both sigma*=1 and sigma*=-1 achieve the same minimum, so sigma* is not unique. The algorithm is therefore not well-defined as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Allow either sign when a tie occurs, or specify a tie-breaking convention.
issues.overall_effect: The algorithmic step is ambiguous, though a trivial tie-breaking rule would fix it.
issues.title: Algorithm claims uniqueness of sigma* but ties occur
issues.why_classification: A short local tie-breaking rule resolves the ambiguity without affecting the construction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: G^j:=[t_j, t_j^\delta],\quad  I^j:=[t_j^\delta, t_{j+1}], \quad B^j:=G^j\cup I^j=[t_j,t_{j+1}],

issues.failure_explanation: If x is in a gap, its distance to the nearest interval center in that coordinate is at most (h+delta)/2=(N+1)delta/2, not N delta/2. For boundary rows, e.g., c_q^{-1}=0 and c_q^0=(h+delta)/2+(q-1)delta, the distance can be (3N-1)delta/2, exceeding N delta. Thus the displayed bound and the analogous |s_{k+1}-s_k| bound are false for some points/rows, so the explicit constant in eqref{approximA} is not established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace N delta by the correct O(N delta) distances (e.g., (N+1)delta/2 or (3N-1)delta/2) and adjust the constant in the theorem.
issues.overall_effect: The main theorem's explicit constant is not proved; the order O(h^alpha) may survive with larger constants.
issues.title: MainResult proof uses underestimated center distances
issues.why_classification: The error is a constant-factor overestimate in distance bounds; a local correction preserves the convergence order and main guarantee.
